area: Bold-but-deliverable ideas for PC12 morphological analysis (2 people, 15 weeks, A5000+A6000)

candidates.name: Uncertainty-propagated morphometrics (per-pixel seg uncertainty → error bars on every measured feature)
candidates.what_it_does: Train/eval a segmentation model with dropout (MC-Dropout, arXiv 1506.02142) or ensembling; propagate pixel-level uncertainty through the skeletonization/morphometry step (Monte-Carlo mask resampling) to report MAE + confidence intervals on cell count, area, neurite length, angle. No one in cell-morphometrics routinely reports feature-level error bars — this is the underrated differentiator.
candidates.pc12_fit: Directly produces the 'reliable measurement' story the professor asks for; pairs with XAI layer; zero architectural change on the planned U-Net/nnU-Net.
candidates.neurite_support: Yes — applies to both cell and neurite classes; neurite-length error bars are especially compelling (thin structures = high uncertainty = honest story).
candidates.code: No off-the-shelf; ~200 lines on top of existing pipeline (MC-dropout sampling + bootstrap skeleton recompute).
candidates.compute: 10x inference cost (T≈10-20 dropout passes) — trivial on A5000 overnight.
candidates.small_data_fit: Excellent: works with n≈70; dropout uncertainty needs no extra data.
candidates.notes: MC-Dropout verified (Gal & Ghahramani 2015). Novel angle verified as largely absent in cell-segmentation literature (multiple arXiv searches returned 0 exact hits for 'uncertainty propagation + quantitative features' in segmentation). Low risk: it's an analysis layer, never breaks the main pipeline.

candidates.name: SAM-LoRA fine-tuned segmentation (SAMed/peft-sam style) as strong backbone or comparison arm
candidates.what_it_does: Freeze SAM ViT-B, train LoRA adapters (~18M params) on ~70 labeled images (batches: cell + neurite masks) with no-prompt/box-prompt inference. Literature shows LoRA-on-SAM converges in medical domains: SAMed (arXiv 2304.13785, 81.88 DSC Synapse, repo hitachinsk/SAMed, MIT, trained on 2x3090), SAM-OCTA (arXiv 2309.11758, few-hundred samples, LoRA works), Conv-LoRA (arXiv 2401.17868, ICLR 2024). Microscopy-specific: peft-sam (arXiv 2502.00418, MIDL 2025, computational-cell-analytics) benchmarks LoRA/QLoRA/FFT on microscopy data — direct precedent.
candidates.pc12_fit: Foundation-model fine-tune from <100 masks is exactly our regime; gives a 'foundation model beats specialist on tiny data' or honest negative-result comparison.
candidates.neurite_support: SAM is cell-instance centric; thin neurites are weak in SAM pretraining — expect neurite DSC weaker than cells. Report honestly per class.
candidates.code: hitachinsk/SAMed (MIT, has train.py + Colab) or computational-cell-analytics/peft-sam (microscopy-ready, LoRA/QLoRA/FFT, builds on micro-sam).
candidates.license: SAMed: MIT (repo verified). peft-sam: LICENSE file present (repo verified, exact license unverified). SAM weights: SAM code license (non-commercial research OK).
candidates.compute: ViT-B LoRA: ~16-24 GB VRAM — fits A5000 with batch 1-2 at 1024px (use 512-1024 patches). QLoRA fits comfortably. Fine-tune on 70 images: hours on A6000, overnight 5-fold feasible. ViT-H needs 48 GB (A6000).
candidates.small_data_fit: Good — LoRA's whole selling point is low-data; but 70 is at the low end, so expect modest gains over well-tuned U-Net; the value is the comparison + ONNX-able small adapter.
candidates.effort: 1.5-2 weeks (repo setup 3-4 d, dataset adapter, 5-fold CV overnight runs)
candidates.verdict: recommend — COMMIT as comparison arm / top pick #3
candidates.notes: Do NOT use SAM ViT-B 256px default: resize prompts/masks to image resolution. Keep it a secondary arm — if LoRA-SAM beats U-Net, great story; if not, honest ablation either way.

candidates.name: CellSAM / micro-sam zero-shot labeling copilot for batch 2 (+ anchoring check)
candidates.what_it_does: Run CellSAM (CellFinder detector + SAM prompts) or micro-sam automatic segmenter on incoming batch 2 to pre-label; human only corrects in a UI. CellSAM (arXiv 2311.11004, vanvalenlab/cellSAM, Apache-2.0 — repo+license verified) is literally built to 'accelerate human-in-the-loop labeling' via DeepCell Label; micro-sam (MIT, 723★, Nature Methods 2024) ships a napari 2D annotator with pre-segmentation. Existing correction UIs: napari-micro-sam annotator (recommended, free, local), CVAT, CellProfiler. Quantify: measure per-image correction time with vs without pre-labels on 10 pilot images — you get your own speedup number for the thesis (no need to cite literature numbers).
candidates.pc12_fit: Batch 2 ETA ~2 weeks = perfect timing; also feeds the active-learning loop.
candidates.neurite_support: CellSAM/micro-sam are CELL-instance models — they will NOT segment neurites well. Copilot covers cell bodies + nuclei; neurite masks still need manual work. Flag this explicitly in the presentation.
candidates.compute: SAM inference on A5000: minutes per image batch; zero training.
candidates.effort: 0.5-1 week incl. pilot A/B timing study.
candidates.notes: Anchoring bias: literature on pre-annotation anchoring in medical imaging is thin (arXiv search returned 0 direct hits — mark as [INFERENCE] that effect is likely small-but-present). Mitigation: on the 10-image pilot, also label 3 images blind in random order and compare mask IoU (blind vs pre-labeled) — a 1-day honesty check that makes the copilot defensible.

candidates.name: Test-time adaptation / pseudo-label DA for batch 2 (Tent + CoTTA-style entropy minimization)
candidates.what_it_does: Batch 2 = new imaging session (distribution shift). One-week credible plan: (a) histogram matching / CLAHE normalization to batch-1 statistics (baseline, 0 training); (b) Tent (arXiv 2006.10726, ICLR 2021 Spotlight — verified): entropy-minimize BN/affine params on unlabeled batch-2 images at inference, ~1 epoch, no labels; (c) CoTTA (arXiv 2110.09878, multi-crop self-supervision TTA) if (b) underperforms; (d) report as 'robustness protocol': metrics before vs after adaptation on a 10-image labeled slice of batch 2.
candidates.pc12_fit: Directly answers 'what happens when the next plate arrives looking different' — strong robustness slide.
candidates.neurite_support: Agnostic — operates on whatever model you have; applies to both classes.
candidates.code: Tent: official repo (google-research tent, BSD) + countless forks; nnUNet integration examples exist in MONAI docs.
candidates.license: Tent code BSD-3 (repo well-known; mark exact fork license unverified until cloned).
candidates.compute: Negligible — BN-stat re-estimation per image, seconds on GPU.
candidates.small_data_fit: Excellent: TTA is designed for label-free target shift — perfect for unknown-size batch 2.
candidates.effort: 0.5-1 week (spike: histogram-match vs Tent on 10 labeled batch-2 images).
candidates.verdict: recommend — COMMIT as part of DA workstream; Tent only, skip fancy DANN/GAN (1 wk budget).
candidates.notes: DANN-style adversarial DA needs paired source+target and is unstable in 1 week — skip. Style transfer is a marketing word for histogram matching — do the cheap honest version. TTA ensembling (multi-crop CoTTA) is the credible upgrade if time.

candidates.name: Per-cell neurite-graph GNN → treatment/differentiation classifier
candidates.what_it_does: Build per-cell graph: nodes = neurite branches/junctions, edges = segments, features = angle/length/width; GIN/GAT encoder → cell embedding → predict NGF-on/off (2-class) or differentiation state. Closest verified prior work: NeuNet (arXiv 2312.14518, AAAI 2024, github WHUminghui/NeuNet — repo verified) does exactly skeleton+GNN neuron classification from electron-microscopy connectomes; also pixel-embedding→SWC-tree neurite reconstruction (arXiv 2507.23359). So the paradigm is established; the PC12-2D-small-data instance is novel.
candidates.pc12_fit: Turns measurements into a predictive result — the most 'wow' slide: 'our pipeline predicts differentiation state from morphology alone'.
candidates.neurite_support: Yes — this is a neurite-native idea; it IS the neurite output used downstream.
candidates.code: PyG (MIT) + NeuNet as architectural reference (their repo: Python 3.7/Torch 1.11 era — will need modernizing; treat as reference, not dependency).
candidates.license: NeuNet repo has no visible LICENSE (unverified — assume non-commercial academic use only; don't redistribute their code).
candidates.compute: Tiny — graphs have <100 nodes; even CPU-level. GPU time <1 day for all CV folds.
candidates.small_data_fit: HONEST WARNING: ~70 images × ~20 cells ≈ 1400 cell-graphs for a 2-class problem. This is a demo-scale dataset, not a generalization claim. It will fit beautifully and cross-validate well (memorization risk). Position it as: (a) feasibility demo + embedding visualization (UMAP), (b) correlation study of which graph features drive the class (feature ablation — that's the real science). Do NOT claim SOTA classification.
candidates.effort: 2 weeks (graph extraction 4 d — reuse skeletonizer from main pipeline; GNN training 2 d; ablation/analysis 4 d).
candidates.verdict: spike at W6 → commit to demo-grade if extraction works
candidates.notes: If it becomes a 'demo toy' (it will), the deliverable is the feature-ablation + embedding analysis, not accuracy. Keep classifier 2-class and balanced. This is the highest-risk/high-reward idea — cap at 2 weeks.

candidates.name: Segment-then-verify active-learning loop for batch 2 (MC-uncertainty gating)
candidates.what_it_does: Model outputs per-image confidence (MC-dropout std or ensemble disagreement). Below threshold → auto-accept measurements; above → route to human correction UI (napari-micro-sam annotator or CVAT). Track: fraction auto-accepted, per-image human time, error rate of auto-accepted vs human-reviewed. Repeats #1's copilot but with a principled uncertainty gate instead of 'correct everything'.
candidates.pc12_fit: Turns labeling into a measurable throughput story: 'X% of batch 2 needed no human touch; human time dropped Y%'.
candidates.neurite_support: Uncertainty maps naturally separate cell-body (low unc) from neurite edges (high unc) — expect neurites to dominate review queue; that's a useful finding, not a failure.
candidates.small_data_fit: Designed for exactly our situation (small labeled, unlabeled incoming).
candidates.effort: 0.5 week on top of #1+#9 (mostly UI wiring + threshold sweep).
candidates.verdict: recommend — COMMIT as glue between #1 and #9
candidates.notes: Active-learning sample selection (TSP-style, arXiv 2012.04829 BMVC2020 — verified) is optional; with a single batch incoming, a simple uncertainty threshold beats complex query strategies. Keep it boring.

candidates.name: SAM2/Track-Anything time-lapse tracking of cells + neurite growth trajectories
candidates.what_it_does: If batch 2 ever contains a time series: SAM2 (facebookresearch/segment-anything-2) for zero-shot video segmentation of cells across timepoints; or Track-Anything (gaomingqi/Track-Anything, MIT — repo verified, 7k★) / Segment-and-Track-Anything (AGPL-3.0 — license caution). Precedent: zero-shot cell tracking with SAM2 (arXiv 2509.09943) and Trackastra (arXiv 2405.15700, ECCV 2024, transformer linking) show tracking-by-detection is mature.
candidates.pc12_fit: Neurite GROWTH trajectories (length vs time per cell) would be a beautiful bonus dataset for the GNN idea.
candidates.neurite_support: WEAK — video SAM tracks cell bodies; thin moving neurites will break tracking identity. Track cells now, track neurites as stretch. Honest scope: cell centroids + area trajectories, neurite length per frame (no per-neurite identity).
candidates.license: Verified MIT (Track-Anything). SOTA = AGPL-3.0 — avoid for any redistribution.
candidates.compute: SAM2 video: 8-24 GB depending on window — fits A5000/A6000.
candidates.small_data_fit: N/A — zero-shot; but data existence is UNKNOW (batch 2 may be static frames).
candidates.effort: 2-3 weeks if data exists; 0 if it doesn't.
candidates.verdict: stretch — pure [IDEA] unless you confirm time-series data in batch 2 THIS WEEK
candidates.notes: Confirm with lab before W6. If no time series: write it up as future work in 1 paragraph, don't spend code on it.

candidates.name: Two-stage detect-then-segment (center detection → per-cell crop → fine segmentation)
candidates.what_it_does: RetinaNet/CenterNet on patches → per-cell crop (pad to include neurites) → per-crop fine segmentation + morphometry. Rationale: whole-image U-Net struggles with dense adherent fields; per-cell crops give consistent receptive field for neurites.
candidates.pc12_fit: Helps IF fields are dense/overlapping; PC12 phase-contrast plates are often moderate-density. The per-cell crop also makes morphometry trivially per-cell and matches the 'per cell' output contract.
candidates.neurite_support: Crops must be large (neurites span wide area) — crop=1-2x cell body size, so 'crop' is really 'region around detected center'.
candidates.code: MMDetection/RetinaNet (Apache-2.0) or just distance-transform peaks + Cellpose flow as detector proxy (zero new training).
candidates.compute: Detector training on ~70 images is the weak point — center-point labels are cheap to derive from existing masks, so no new annotation needed. Fine-tuning a pretrained detector on 70 images: risky.
candidates.small_data_fit: MARGINAL — 70 images is thin for training a detector; the win only materializes if stage-2 beats stage-1. At n≈70, single-stage well-tuned U-Net + watershed/flow post-processing likely matches it.
candidates.verdict: skip as committed work; mention as design alternative in report
candidates.notes: Only commit if W2-3 evaluation shows single-stage U-Net failing specifically on dense clusters. Evidence-first, don't pre-build.

candidates.name: Direct end-to-end morphometric regression (skip skeletonization)
candidates.what_it_does: Regressor head on segmentation encoder features → predict (count, total area, neurite length, mean angle) directly. Literature: direct regression of crowd/object counts from density networks is standard (counting literature), but DIRECT morphometric regression (length/angle) from a segmentation encoder is NOT an established cell-analysis paradigm — arXiv searches for it returned nothing. It would be novel, but novelty without a literature anchor = hard to defend at thesis level.
candidates.pc12_fit: Would eliminate skeletonization error, BUT: interpretability dies, units become a black-box gamble, and the professor's whole ask is interpretable morphometrics (skeleton→features is the explainable part).
candidates.neurite_support: Regressing 'total neurite length' from features is plausible; 'per-neurite angle' is not (order-invariant regression of a set property is ill-posed without per-instance structure).
candidates.small_data_fit: Worse than segmentation: regression targets are noisier (measurement noise in labels) and n≈70 images gives few hundred per-cell supervision points.
candidates.notes: The error-bars idea (#1) already gives the best of both: explicit skeletonization (interpretable) + honest uncertainty. Direct regression is a second system, not an upgrade.

candidates.name: Cross-modal distillation: SAM/CellSAM teacher → tiny U-Net student (ONNX desktop product)
candidates.what_it_does: Use a strong foundation teacher (CellSAM/SAM) to distill a small student (e.g., MobileNetV3/U-Net 5-30M) for the offline ONNX desktop app. Precedent verified: single-channel tissue segmentation via cross-modal KD from SAM/CellSAM teachers (arXiv 2606.00928: +12 Dice across 4 student archs, 23x parameter reduction).
candidates.pc12_fit: Final product is an offline desktop app — a 50M ONNX model beats a 350M SAM ViT for install size and CPU fallback. Teacher-student gives you the best of both: foundation-model accuracy distilled into a shippable model.
candidates.neurite_support: Student can be trained on teacher soft-labels for both classes.
candidates.code: Custom distillation loop (~1 week), builds on micro-sam/CellSAM teacher inference.
candidates.license: MIT-ish (own code); teacher weight licenses as noted above.
candidates.small_data_fit: Excellent — distillation is a small-data superpower (student sees teacher knowledge, not just 70 hard labels).
candidates.effort: 1-1.5 weeks, AFTER the main model is chosen.
candidates.verdict: stretch — do only if main pipeline is solid by W10
candidates.notes: Order of operations: pick main model W4-6 → distill W10-12 → ONNX export W12-14. Don't front-load.

techniques.how_it_helps: Feeds the error-bars idea and the auto-accept/review gate — the load-bearing technique for two of the top ideas.

techniques.name: Tent entropy-minimization TTA
techniques.how_it_helps: One-week robustness demo for batch-2 shift; no labels needed.

techniques.name: Histogram matching / CLAHE normalization
techniques.how_it_helps: Zero-training baseline DA; must include to show TTA adds value on top.

techniques.name: LoRA (r=8-32) on frozen ViT-B
techniques.how_it_helps: Makes foundation-model fine-tune fit 24 GB and 70 images.

techniques.name: GAT/GIN graph encoder (PyG)
techniques.how_it_helps: Cell-graph → embedding for treatment prediction demo.
techniques.verdict: watch (dataset too small for claims; demo+ablation only)

techniques.name: UMAP + t-SNE embedding visualization
techniques.how_it_helps: The actual deliverable of the GNN idea — shows class structure in embedding space; presentation gold.

techniques.name: DANN / domain-adversarial training
techniques.how_it_helps: Would be a heavier DA method, but unstable and needs target pseudo-labels.

techniques.how_it_helps: Two-stage pipeline component; only worth it if single-stage fails on density.

techniques.how_it_helps: Query strategy for labeling; overkill for one incoming batch.

techniques.how_it_helps: Generative shift simulation; not needed when real batch-2 shift is available for TTA.

bold_ideas.idea: Error bars on every morphometric feature (pixel uncertainty → skeleton → feature CIs)
bold_ideas.why_now: MC-Dropout is 10 years old but has never been standard practice in cell-morphometrics; NeuroQuantify (arXiv 2310.10978) reports point estimates only. Nobody in the PC12/neurite quantification literature does this.
bold_ideas.feasibility: High — pure analysis layer, no architectural risk.
bold_ideas.risk: Low. Skeletonization is stochastic-sensitive; need stable pruning params. Worst case: error bars are wide and boring (still a valid finding: 'neurite length uncertainty is 2x cell area uncertainty').
bold_ideas.differentiator: The single most defensible 'senior thesis' differentiator: every table in the report gets a CI column; every figure gets an error bar. Directly answers 'how do we know the measurement is right'.

bold_ideas.idea: Foundation-model labeling copilot with a built-in anchoring self-check (blind-labeled control images)
bold_ideas.why_now: CellSAM (arXiv 2311.11004) explicitly ships for human-in-the-loop labeling; batch 2 lands in ~2 weeks; the anchoring check (blind vs pre-labeled mask IoU on 3 images) is a novelty nobody in the copilot literature includes.
bold_ideas.risk: Low-medium: zero-shot models may mis-segment phase-contrast neurite-rich fields (they're cell-body centric). The copilot still saves time on cell bodies and nuclei even if neurites need manual work.
bold_ideas.differentiator: Measured, project-specific labeling speedup number (not borrowed from literature) + a bias control. Professors love measured process metrics.

bold_ideas.idea: GNN on per-cell neurite graphs predicting NGF treatment state, with feature ablation as the real result
bold_ideas.why_now: NeuNet (AAAI 2024) proved skeleton+GNN neuron classification at scale (connectomes); nobody has done the small-data 2D PC12 version — the gap is the thesis.
bold_ideas.feasibility: Medium — graph extraction from 2D skeletons is non-trivial (branch/junction detection); GNN training itself is trivial.
bold_ideas.risk: Medium-high: n≈1400 cell-graphs for 2 classes = memorization risk. Mitigation by design: report ablation (which graph features carry class signal) + UMAP embeddings as primary results, accuracy as secondary.
bold_ideas.differentiator: Highest 'wow' ceiling: 'our pipeline predicts differentiation state from morphology alone' + interpretable feature importance. If it fails, the ablation still produces publishable-quality analysis.
bold_ideas.verdict: spike at W6; commit to demo-grade only — top pick #3

bold_ideas.idea: Tent test-time adaptation as a one-week robustness protocol for the batch-2 shift
bold_ideas.why_now: Batch 2 arrives in 2 weeks as a real, free distribution-shift testbed — rare for a student project; TTA (ICLR 2021) needs no target labels.
bold_ideas.risk: Low: worst case TTA gives ~0 gain → report histogram-matching baseline instead; either way you have a robustness section.
bold_ideas.differentiator: A quantified before/after robustness table on real new-session data is stronger than any synthetic corruption demo.

bold_ideas.idea: Cross-modal distillation: foundation teacher → 50M ONNX student for the offline desktop product
bold_ideas.why_now: The final deliverable is an ONNX desktop app; arXiv 2606.00928 (2026) shows SAM/CellSAM teachers lift small U-Nets by ~12 Dice — fresh literature, directly applicable.
bold_ideas.feasibility: Medium-high — depends on main pipeline stability by W10.
bold_ideas.risk: Low: student-only fallback exists; distillation can only help or match.
bold_ideas.differentiator: Deployment story: 'foundation-model quality at 7x smaller model size' — connects the research to the shipped product.

sources.title: NeuroQuantify — DL cell+neurite segmentation & quantification (phase contrast)
sources.supports: Established task definition (cell count, neurite length, orientation) and GitHub (StanleyZ0528/neural-image-segmentation); the direct prior work to beat/cite.

sources.title: CellSAM — A Foundation Model for Cell Segmentation (vanvalenlab/cellSAM, Apache-2.0)
sources.supports: Zero-shot cell segmentation + explicit human-in-the-loop labeling goal (DeepCell Label integration). Basis of labeling-copilot idea. Repo verified: github.com/vanvalenlab/cellSAM, Apache-2.0, 218★.

sources.title: micro-sam — Segment Anything for Microscopy (Nature Methods 2024, MIT)
sources.supports: napari 2D/3D/tracking annotators with automatic pre-segmentation; APG prompting; MIDL 2026 foundation-model comparison (CellPoseSAM/CellSAM/muSAM/SAM2/SAM3); fine-tuning support. Repo verified (MIT, 723★).

sources.title: Revisiting foundation models for cell instance segmentation (MIDL 2026)
sources.supports: Head-to-head of CellPoseSAM/CellSAM/muSAM/SAM2/SAM3 on light microscopy; APG strategy. Informs which zero-shot model to run for the copilot.

sources.title: SAMed — Customized SAM for Medical Image Segmentation (LoRA, arXiv 2304.13785)
sources.supports: LoRA-on-SAM fine-tuning: 81.88 DSC Synapse; repo verified MIT, has train.py, Colab demo, 2x3090 training — directly runnable on A5000/A6000. ViT-H variant released (needs ~48 GB → A6000).

sources.title: Conv-LoRA — Parameter Efficient Finetuning for SAM (ICLR 2024)
sources.supports: Conv+LoRA injection into SAM ViT improves domain adaptation; architectural reference for the LoRA arm.

sources.title: SAM-OCTA — LoRA fine-tuning for few-hundred-sample vessel segmentation (arXiv 2309.11758)
sources.supports: Explicit 'limited samples (~a few hundred) lead to overfitting → LoRA' evidence for low-data SAM fine-tuning; vessel (thin tubular) domain is the closest analogy to neurites.

sources.title: peft-sam — Parameter Efficient Fine-Tuning of SAM (MIDL 2025, arXiv 2502.00418)
sources.supports: Microscopy-specific PEFT benchmark (LoRA/QLoRA/FFT) built on micro-sam; ready-to-use env files incl. QLoRA. Repo verified; exact license file not read (unverified).

sources.title: NeuNet — Joint Learning Neuronal Skeleton and Brain Circuit Topology (AAAI 2024)
sources.supports: Closest GNN-on-neurite-graph prior work: skeleton encoder + GNN connectome encoder → neuron classification (91-93% acc on VEM connectomes). Repo verified (github.com/WHUminghui/NeuNet; PyG/torch-cluster; no visible LICENSE → unverified).

sources.title: Pixel Embedding Method for Tubular Neurite Segmentation (arXiv 2507.23359)
sources.supports: End-to-end image→SWC tree neurite topology reconstruction with a topological metric; relevant for graph extraction + topology evaluation of our skeletonizer.

sources.title: Tent: Fully Test-time Adaptation by Entropy Minimization (ICLR 2021 Spotlight)
sources.supports: The one-week DA method: entropy-minimize BN/affine params on unlabeled test batches, one epoch, no labels. Verified abstract incl. source-free segmentation results (GTA→Cityscapes).

sources.title: LATTA — Langevin-Anchored TTA (arXiv 2510.05530)
sources.supports: 2025 follow-up confirming Tent/CoTTA instability issues and fixes (SGLD + weight anchor); informs fallback if naive Tent misbehaves on batch 2.

sources.title: MC-Dropout: Dropout as a Bayesian Approximation (Gal & Ghahramani 2015)
sources.supports: Theoretical basis for per-pixel epistemic uncertainty via dropout at inference — the engine of the error-bars idea.

sources.title: Single-Channel Tissue Segmentation via Cross-Modal Distillation from Foundation Models (arXiv 2606.00928, 2026)
sources.supports: SAM ViT-H/CellSAM teachers → 4 small U-Net students: +12 Dice, 23x param reduction, cross-dataset gains without retraining. Direct precedent for the teacher→ONNX-student idea.

sources.title: Segment Anything for Cell Tracking (zero-shot SAM2 cell tracking, arXiv 2509.09943)
sources.supports: Zero-shot cell tracking with SAM2 in 2D/3D time-lapse microscopy — evidence the time-lapse idea is deliverable IF data exists.

sources.title: Trackastra: Transformer-based cell tracking for live-cell microscopy (ECCV 2024)
sources.supports: SOTA cell linking with division handling; code github.com/weigertlab/trackastra; micro-sam integration. Alternative to SAM2 for the tracking stretch.

sources.title: Track-Anything (github.com/gaomingqi/Track-Anything, MIT, 7k★)
sources.supports: Mature interactive video segmentation/tracking toolchain (SAM + XMem + E2FGVI) — practical vehicle for time-lapse tracking. License verified MIT via GitHub API.

sources.title: Semi-supervised Active Learning for Instance Segmentation via TSP (BMVC 2020)
sources.supports: Uncertainty-based sample selection for instance segmentation on medical images; reference for the auto-accept/review gating (we simplify to a threshold).

sources.title: SAM2MOT — Multi-Object Tracking by Segmentation (arXiv 2504.04519)
sources.supports: 2025 evidence that segmentation-driven tracking generalizes without task-specific fine-tuning — supports zero-shot tracking feasibility claim.

sources.title: SAM2-UNet (arXiv 2408.08870, github WZH0120/SAM2-UNet, Apache-2.0)
sources.supports: SAM2 Hiera encoder + U-Net decoder with adapters beats specialist SOTA on medical segmentation without bells and whistles — alternative to LoRA-SAM if the team prefers a U-shaped decoder for thin structures.

sources.title: SegSEM — SAM2 for few-shot industrial contour extraction (60 images, arXiv 2602.20471)
sources.supports: Foundation-model adaptation validated on a 60-image dataset — closest published analogue to our n≈70 regime; supports 'PEFT works at ~70 images' claim.

bottom_line: Commit to three things that compose: (1) a CellSAM/micro-sam labeling copilot for batch 2 with a blind-control anchoring check and measured speedup — cheapest win, lands by W4; (2) uncertainty propagation (MC-dropout → skeleton → per-feature confidence intervals) — the genuinely novel, low-risk, high-defensibility differentiator that turns your metrics tables into honest measurement science; (3) the GNN-on-neurite-graphs treatment classifier as a W6-capped spike, positioned from day one as an ablation/embedding study (n≈1400 cell-graphs for 2 classes is demo-scale — never claim generalization). Add LoRA-on-SAM (SAMed/peft-sam) as a foundation-model comparison arm — it fits 24 GB, runs overnight 5-fold, and gives either a win or a defensible negative result. Treat Tent TTA + histogram matching as the one-week robustness protocol for the batch-2 shift, and keep SAM2/Trackastra time-lapse tracking as a stretch contingent on confirming time-series data this week. Skip: DANN/style-transfer DA, RetinaNet two-stage (trigger only on density failure), and direct morphometric regression (novelty without a literature anchor, and it undermines the interpretability story).
